name: Regulated lithium-ion
summary: Regulated lithium-ion cells, sold as 1.5 V rechargeable lithium AA and AAA batteries, house a 3.7 V lithium-ion cell and a buck converter that holds the output at 1.5 V. Voltage stays nearly constant until the electronics shut the cell down, and some charge through a built-in USB port.
body:
## How it works

A regulated lithium-ion cell is a lithium-ion cell plus electronics in an AA or AAA case. Wikipedia describes the first widely sold example, the Kentli PH5, as a AA-size housing containing a rechargeable 3.7 V lithium-ion cell and an internal buck converter at the positive terminal that reduces the output to 1.5 V. A protection circuit is part of the design: Ansmann's datasheet states that its circuitry protects against overcharging, overload, short circuit and deep discharge. Because the electronics set the terminal voltage, this entry describes behavior at the terminals rather than a single cell chemistry.

## Discharge behavior

Output stays at 1.5 V with virtually no drop over the discharge, unlike alkaline or NiMH cells. Ansmann specifies a stable 1.5 V over 95% of the runtime, then a drop to 1.1 V at about 5% remaining capacity to signal that the battery needs charging; XTAR describes a 1.1 V low-power indication. Current is limited by the converter: both Ansmann and XTAR give a 2 A maximum continuous discharge current. A device that reads battery voltage to estimate remaining charge sees little change until the final drop.

Ansmann rates its AA at 2000 mAh (minimum 1800 mAh) and 3.26 Wh; XTAR rates its AA at 2450 mAh and 4100 mWh. Ansmann lists up to 1,500 charge cycles and XTAR 1,200. Ansmann specifies operation from −20 to 60 °C and storage from −20 to 25 °C; XTAR specifies operation and storage from −20 to 50 °C and charging from 0 to 45 °C. Wikipedia gives self-discharge of 3% per month for the Kentli cell.

## Uses

Devices designed for 1.5 V primary cells that run poorly on the 1.2 V of NiMH. Ansmann lists electric toys, flashlights, radios, measuring devices, security cameras, soap dispensers and electric door locks.

## History

Kentli has sold its PH5 since 2014. The Kentli design exposes the internal 3.7 V electrode in a ring around the AA terminal so that a dedicated charger can reach it. By 2023, several brands sold 1.5 V lithium-ion cells in both AA and AAA sizes. Some need a special charger, since a charger for 1.2 V cells will not supply sufficient voltage, and others have a USB port built into the cell; Ansmann's AA charges through USB-C at 350 mA.

## Status

Current. No IEC designation for these cells appears in the sources consulted.
strengths: Constant 1.5 V output over about 95% of runtime (Ansmann)
Low self-discharge: about 3% per month (Wikipedia, Kentli)
limitations: Converter limits current, typically 2 A maximum
Abrupt end of runtime; voltage-based gauges give little warning
A charger for 1.2 V cells does not supply sufficient voltage (Wikipedia)
safety: Relies on built-in protection circuitry against overcharge, overload, short circuit and deep discharge
Charge only with the method the manufacturer specifies

sources.title: Li-Ion batteries AA type 2000 (min. 1800 mAh) product datasheet, 1312-0036
